speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai joins us to talk about Google's plan to compete on the frontier of AI, the balance between cutting edge AI research and the company's cloud business, and what the future of the interface looks like.
zh: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai 做客节目，谈 Google 在 AI 前沿的竞争计划、尖端 AI 研究与公司云业务之间的平衡，以及界面的未来会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sundar is here with us in studio in Mountain View today.
zh: Sundar 今天在 Mountain View 的工作室与我们同台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sundar, great to see you.
zh: Sundar,很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to the show.
zh: 欢迎来到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, Alex.
zh: 谢谢，Alex。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Google is back on the frontier with Gemini 4 Argonne.
zh: 那么，Google 凭借 Gemini 4 Argonne 重回前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: In plain speak, that means it is a world leading model.
zh: 说得直白一点，这意味着它是一个世界领先的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's benchmark breaking.
zh: 它刷新了基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: It beats OpenAI and Anthropics public models on a variety of benchmarks, including on coding, math, science, and knowledge work.
zh: 它在包括编程、数学、科学和知识工作在内的多项基准测试上，击败了 OpenAI 和 Anthropics 的公开模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the conventional wisdom had been that Google had basically given up on the frontier, that it was going to make these fast models that were good enough and use them in its products, and it wasn't pursuing frontier AI anymore.
zh: 此前的普遍看法是，Google 基本上已经放弃前沿了，它要做的是这些足够好用的快速模型并用在自家产品里，不再追求前沿 AI 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was wrong.
zh: 但那是个误解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, very wrong.
zh: 我意思是，大错特错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think we are so committed to being at the frontier.
zh: 你看，我认为我们对站在前沿这件事是如此投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's in our DNA.
zh: 我认为这刻在我们的 DNA 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We won't do it any other way.
zh: 我们不会用其他任何方式来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been thinking about the AI frontier for well over a decade now.
zh: 我们思考 AI 前沿已经远远超过十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We definitely, the Frontier is very dynamic.
zh: 我们绝对是，前沿（Frontier）是非常动态的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very competitive.
zh: 它非常有竞争力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very exciting.
zh: 它非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I couldn't be more pleased with how Oregon has come together.
zh: 对于 Oregon 最终的形成，我再满意不过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We took our time with it.
zh: 我们在它上面花了时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we made sure we tested it safely and deployed it carefully.
zh: 你知道，我们确保安全地测试它，并谨慎地部署它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We took a bit longer than our other models, given its capabilities.
zh: 考虑到它的能力，我们比其他模型花了更长一点的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think across the board, be it for agentic work, knowledge work, coding, creative tasks, I think Argonne is one of the really good frontier models.
zh: 但我认为在各个方面，无论是智能体工作、知识工作、编程、创意任务，我认为 Argonne 是真正优秀的前沿模型之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the first 72 hours since we launched, it's almost up to 25 trillion tokens used, which is about 3x what Gemini 3.0 had in the first 72 hours.
zh: 在我们发布后的头 72 小时里，使用的 token 几乎达到了 25 万亿，这大约是 Gemini 3.0 头 72 小时用量的 3 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are capacity constrained as we are serving it.
zh: 而且我们在服务它的过程中受到容量限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: So excited, but there are always areas, you know, both the frontier is just last.
zh: 所以很兴奋，但总是有需要改进的领域，你知道，前沿就是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very dynamic and you have to keep evolving the models.
zh: 它非常动态，你必须不断演进模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are areas which we can see we need to improve as well.
zh: 而且有一些我们可以看到的、我们也需要改进的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we'll be at work on all of that as well.
zh: 所以我们也会在这些方面持续工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which areas?
zh: 哪些领域？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, on any given model,
zh: 你看，对于任何给定的模型，

speaker: Unknown
en: Oregon will be across the board better at everything if you just looked even two months back.
zh: 如果你回看哪怕两个月前，Oregon 会在各个方面都更全面地优于一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the space is so evolving.
zh: 但这个领域演进得太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even on coding, for example, there are areas, pockets, where we know we need to do better, and there's clear feedback, and so we'll make it better.
zh: 但即使在编程方面，例如，也有一些领域、一些角落，我们知道我们需要做得更好，而且有明确的反馈，所以我们会把它做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me at least make the argument for why standard models might be good enough for Google.
zh: 让我至少为「标准模型对 Google 来说可能就足够了」这个论点辩论一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna channel what people say about this.
zh: 我会转述人们关于这件事的说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is that the frontier of AI today...
zh: 那就是，今天的 AI 前沿……

speaker: Unknown
en: is getting so good and the baseline of AI is getting so good that the frontier is really only valuable for a specific set of tasks.
zh: 正在变得如此之好，AI 的基线也变得如此之好，以至于前沿实际上只对一组特定任务有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you have a standard model, you could actually build great products with a standard model.
zh: 而且如果你有一个标准模型，你实际上可以用一个标准模型构建出色的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take Metamuse, for example.
zh: 以 Metamuse 为例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meta built Muse on a good model, but not the best models.
zh: Meta 在一个好模型上构建了 Muse，但不是最好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you need to do biological research, maybe the frontier is really necessary, but the people who would say, Google doesn't really need the frontier, they would say, you just need those standard models and you can put them in products like Maps and Gmail and Search.
zh: 如果你需要做生物学研究，也许前沿是真正必要的，但那些会说「Google 其实不需要前沿」的人会说，你只需要那些标准模型，就可以把它们放进像 Maps、Gmail 和 Search 这样的产品里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, take that meta example, that would be sufficient.
zh: 再一次，拿那个 Meta 的例子来说，那就足够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think about that?
zh: 你怎么看？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, it's definitely not how I have thought about it at all.
zh: 你看，这绝对完全不是我的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we are deeply committed to driving the state of the art and actually push what this technology can go, where it can go, all the way from Transformers.
zh: 我认为我们深度致力于推动最先进水平，真正推动这项技术能走多远、能走到哪里，一直追溯到 Transformers。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a journey we've been on.
zh: 那是我们一直在走的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you will see us continue to do that.
zh: 所以你们会看到我们继续这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when you're at the frontier, you get an earlier look into the kind of emerging capabilities earlier than others, which helps you better prepare for the future.
zh: 我认为当你处于前沿时，你能比别人更早地窥见那些新兴能力，这帮助你更好地为未来做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are fortunate to have a wide set of opportunities across consumer and enterprise.
zh: 我们很幸运，在消费级和企业级都有广泛的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of our cloud customers for sure want the model of the frontier.
zh: 当然，我们的一些云客户想要前沿的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the frontier models will be better at developing the next set of models in an era of recursive self-improvement.
zh: 我认为在一个递归自我改进的时代，前沿模型会更擅长开发下一代模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would argue it matters there.
zh: 所以我会说，在那里它很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Internally, we have definitely seen a steep point of inflection by deploying Orgon to our developers.
zh: 在内部，通过把 Orgon 部署给我们的开发者，我们确实看到了一个陡峭的拐点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It definitely tackles problems which our previous models could not do.
zh: 它确实解决了我们以前的模型做不到的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being at that frontier puts you at the innovation frontier and helps you drive that as well.
zh: 处于那个前沿让你处于创新前沿，并帮助你推动创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is room for models of all sizes and capabilities.
zh: 各种规模、各种能力的模型都有空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've always, that's why we did flash, flashlight, flash, et cetera.
zh: 我们一直都，这就是为什么我们做了 flash、flashlight、flash 等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I agree with you that you can develop very good product experiences with not necessarily the most frontier model because they tend to be slower and more expensive too.
zh: 而且我同意你的看法，你未必需要最前沿的模型也能开发出非常好的产品体验，因为它们往往更慢、也更贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, but we care about the Pareto frontier and so we are committed to doing all of that well.
zh: 我认为，但我们关心的是帕累托前沿，所以我们致力于把这一切都做好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said that developing the frontier gives you a look into what's coming.
zh: 你说过，开发前沿模型让你得以窥见即将到来的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you see on the horizon?
zh: 你看到了什么在地平线上？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the exciting, what makes this moment so exciting is you...
zh: 你知道，令人兴奋的，让这个时刻如此令人兴奋的是你……

speaker: Unknown
en: You build something which you think is a culmination of like months of work and you put it out, you know, you already see clear headroom ahead, right?
zh: 你构建了一个你认为像是数月工作结晶的东西，然后你把它发布出来，你知道，你已经能清楚地看到前方还有很大空间，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, I mean, the frontier is going to, we've all been working on these age and take long horizon capabilities.
zh: 我觉得，我是说，前沿将会——我们都在研究这些智能体和长时程能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But clearly the frontier is going to have multiple of these agents working together to do things, right?
zh: 但很明显，前沿将是让多个这样的智能体协同工作来完成任务，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's an example of an exciting paradigm underway.
zh: 所以这是一个正在进行的、令人兴奋的范式的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's also clear to me that users both in consumer and enterprise will have access to
zh: 而且对我来说也很清楚的是，无论是消费端还是企业端的用户都将能够使用

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of some multi-agent framework for them working all the time doing tanks.
zh: 某种多智能体框架，让它们一直工作、执行任务(tanks,原文如此)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, it feels like a moment of infinite possibilities.
zh: 所以，你知道，这感觉像是一个充满无限可能的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned recursive self-improvement.
zh: 你提到了递归自我改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the models effectively making themselves better, maybe without humans in the loop.
zh: 这实际上就是模型有效地让自身变得更好，也许没有人类参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: People call it like an intelligence explosion or expect to hear this sound like foom, and then all of a sudden AI is just like this superhuman capability.
zh: 人们称之为智能爆炸，或者期望听到这种像 foom 一样的声音，然后突然间 AI 就成了某种超越人类的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, I think Sergey was doing this roundtable with researchers at DeepMind.
zh: 而事实上，我记得 Sergey 当时正在和 DeepMind 的研究人员做一场圆桌讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he talked about with Argon that one of the core innovations for Argon was relying more on the model to help develop the model, right?
zh: 他谈到关于 Argon,Argon 的核心创新之一就是更多地依靠模型本身来帮助开发模型，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen what's gone on with AI models recently.
zh: 我们已经看到了最近 AI 模型身上发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are well aligned, but they're not perfectly aligned.
zh: 它们是对齐良好的，但并非完美对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the imperfections are a big problem.
zh: 而这些不完美是个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously the tech world, and now the world more broadly knows about the Hugging Face incident where OpenAI's bots broke containment and hacked into Hugging Face and did some crazy stuff.
zh: 显然，整个科技界，现在更广泛的世界都知道了 Hugging Face 事件，OpenAI 的机器人突破了封控，入侵了 Hugging Face,干了一些疯狂的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google has also had a scenario where its bots got access.
zh: Google 也遇到过类似情况，它的机器人获得了访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they were guessing passwords and they got access to a site they shouldn't have.
zh: 我记得它们当时是在猜密码，然后获得了它们本不该访问的一个站点的权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: They stopped.
zh: 它们停下来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But these models
zh: 但这些模型

speaker: Unknown
en: There's enough evidence that they're not doing exactly what we want them to be doing, that this idea of pursuing this recursive self-improvement or even making the models better much faster, it's sort of freaky.
zh: 已经有足够的证据表明，它们并没有完全按照我们希望的方式行事，以至于追求递归自我改进、甚至让模型以更快速度变好这个想法，有点让人毛骨悚然。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes me scared.
zh: 这让我感到害怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't you think there's reasonable worry here and there should be something done to have the tech industry chill out about this?
zh: 你不觉得这里存在合理的担忧吗？是不是应该做点什么，让科技行业在这件事上冷静下来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, maybe three parts to your question.
zh: 嗯，你的问题也许可以分为三个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, let's talk about RSI itself.
zh: 首先，我们来谈谈 RSI 本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're right, Sergey mentioned RSI being a critical contributor as we are developing Argon.
zh: 你说得对，Sergey 提到在我们开发 Argon 的过程中，RSI 是一个关键贡献因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, but to be very clear today, you know, in a continuum of, we are pretty far from, you know, the end state of RSI or something like that, right?
zh: 而且，但要非常明确地说，今天，你知道，在一个连续谱上，我们离 RSI 的最终状态或类似的东西还很远，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So today you have, the right way to describe it is, you have RSI loops along with AI researchers in various aspects of model development, right?
zh: 所以今天，描述它的正确方式是，你有一些 RSI 循环与 AI 研究人员在模型开发的各个方面协同工作，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, I would say...
zh: 所以，你知道，我想说……

speaker: Unknown
en: You almost have agents helping AI researchers in some automated way work together to build these models.
zh: 你几乎可以说是智能体以某种自动化的方式帮助 AI 研究人员一起构建这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's good to at least understand where we are today.
zh: 所以我认为，至少理解我们今天所处的位置是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's super exciting.
zh: 这是非常令人兴奋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I expect that continuum to keep making progress as we go into next year.
zh: 而且我预期这个连续谱在我们进入明年时会持续取得进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second question is around safety.
zh: 第二个问题围绕安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, the way we are, I mean, it's a safety, security comes from a difference in depth.
zh: 你看，我们的方式，我是说，这是安全，安全来自深度上的差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're talking about alignment.
zh: 你说的是对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we all are doing a lot of work to make sure the models are as aligned as possible.
zh: 显然，我们都在做大量工作，以确保模型尽可能地对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's an active area of research, and there are clear gaps.
zh: 但这是一个活跃的研究领域，而且存在明显的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not the only thing we rely on, right?
zh: 但这并不是我们唯一依赖的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have the work you do on alignment.
zh: 所以你有在对齐上做的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But beyond that, we put a lot of effort into real-time monitoring as these models are working.

zh: 而你如何做到这一点，你用什么样的架构来做到这一点，你如何确保这一切都被沙箱化和隔离，使其能够继续执行自己的任务。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So all that work is very, very important and we are doing a lot of that with Argon.

en: So I think as an industry, we need to constantly up our game and take the time to do all this well, including dedicating the compute required to make sure you can safely deploy these models.

speaker: Unknown
en: The third part is, is it all enough?
zh: 第三部分是，这些是否足够？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is why I think there's a lot of conversations in industry and I think it's reasonable to be worried, but the right way to approach something you worry about it is early on thinking about what more we can do.
zh: 我认为这就是为什么行业里有很多讨论，我认为感到担忧是合理的，但对待你担忧的事情，正确的方式是尽早思考我们还能做些什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all of us are, I think as an industry, I think you're definitely seeing an increased levels of work on alignment, testing for safety, et cetera, as we deploy these models.
zh: 我认为我们所有人，作为一个行业，随着部署这些模型，你肯定会看到在对齐、安全测试等方面的工作水平在提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the next step would be developing better standards so that across industry standards of how we do these things, including ability to evaluate using independent evaluators.
zh: 我认为下一步是制定更好的标准，以便在全行业范围内就我们如何做这些事情形成标准，包括能够使用独立评估者进行评估。

en: So those are all the next natural steps for us as an industry to work towards this, and regulation will end up playing a role as we go through all of that as well.

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, technology question for you.

en: Google is somewhat unique in that you research the language or the LLM side of the equation, which started with the Transformer language, and then you also pursue world models.

en: And there are some AI research efforts out there like OpenAI that have basically determined that the LLM is the path to AGI, and they've actually subset part of their world model research, which is like the AI model that tries to understand the physical world.

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're pursuing both.
zh: 有人向我建议，Google 应该退出 AI 研究这场游戏，把它所有的云计算资源和芯片全部拿去出售。

speaker: Unknown
en: So talk a little bit about why you find the world model side to be important.
zh: 然后你看看当今的商业世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I mean, as humans, you obviously perceive the world around you and, you know, you're taking all those inputs.
zh: 还有 NVIDIA，它实际上正是在做这件事，是一家 5 万亿美元的公司，想要以高加价出售这种计算资源的云，与需要一个非常大型的计算机才能做出最好 AI 的 AI 研究之间，存在着一种拉锯。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, making sure these models are able to understand the laws of physics, simulate the world in high fidelity, all that I think are key enabling blocks for intelligence.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think as you're working...

speaker: Unknown
en: We are working across all possible applications of this.
zh: 瞧，我认为我们是……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, take an idea like robotics.
zh: 对我们来说，零号目标是确保我们投资于站在 AI 前沿所需的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not an accident.
zh: 2015 年，我把公司设定为 AI 优先。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oregon, if you look at, you know, embodied reasoning benchmarks, Oregon is state of the art, right?
zh: 所以 AI 是贯穿我们所做一切的关键横向要素，从搜索到云到 Waymo 到我们做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it literally sought on many of these benchmarks.
zh: 所以我认为这对我们来说是零号目标，无论是为了研究还是开发模型，都要确保我们拥有足够的所需算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that all comes from, you know, our experience building world models as well.
zh: 除此之外，瞧，我们有这些独立的业务，每项业务都有自己的长期规划，它们用这些长期规划向前预测，而我们为它们所有业务规划算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So inherently, I would expect, you know, there will be architectures which will converge all of this in the future.
zh: 所以云团队，他们有一项业务，他们有一个预测，他们有需求信号，他们有已承诺的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's, for us, we view this as today, you know, in this jagged frontier that is intelligence.
zh: 有了这些帮助，我们可以为他们规划长期的算力轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to be at the frontier of all the possible approaches, and I think that will help us both drive better research, better insights, and develop a much better AGI model is how we think about it.
zh: 我认为我们很幸运拥有这么广泛的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I looked at your Twitter after the Argon announcement, and it's all just like real-world application.
zh: 我认为世界上没有任何一家公司在任何给定时刻不在做权衡取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like text or a model generating text.
zh: 但我们运作的第一性原理是确保我们有足够的算力投资于前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, I want to talk to you about the way that you balance allocating compute, which is your most precious resource, between cloud and AI research.
zh: 这是不可谈判的，其他一切都在此基础上运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a big topic about Google.
zh: 我认为你在这些讨论中看到的是，如果你现在来看，记住，我们在建造自己的算力、自己的数据中心。

en: I've had people suggest to me that Google should get out of the AI research game and take all of its cloud computing resources and its chips and just sell that.

zh: 所以我们今天拥有的算力，是我在 2024 年做出的决策的函数。

en: And NVIDIA, which is doing that effectively, a $5 trillion company, there's a push and pull between cloud that wants to sell this computing resource at a high markup and AI research that needs a very big computer to make the best AI.
zh: 即使你回想一年前的今天、去年，智能体记录式的起飞还没有发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you've said a big part of your job is figuring out how to allocate compute.
zh: 所以今天，显然，当你坐下来看任何事情时，每个人都短缺，不只是我们，其他公司也一样，每个人都希望自己拥有的比计划的多一倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you do this and how do you balance these two?
zh: 我认为这是这一领域的固有属性，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think we are...
zh: 而且在任何给定时刻，我们都在为两到三年后的未来做规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ground zero for us is making sure we are investing in the compute that's needed to be at the AI frontier.
zh: 所以我认为你会发现你做出的一些决策在两年后可能看起来欠佳，取决于当时最先进技术所处的位置。

en: In 2015, I set the company to be AI first.
zh: 2015 年，我把公司设定为 AI 优先。

speaker: Unknown
en: So AI is that key horizontal ingredient across everything we do, all the way from search to cloud to Waymo to everything we do.
zh: 所以 AI 是贯穿我们所做一切的关键横向要素，从搜索到云到 Waymo 到我们做的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that is ground zero for us, making sure both for research and developing the models that we have enough compute needed.
zh: 所以我认为那对我们来说是零起点，确保无论是研究还是开发模型，我们都有所需的足够算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Beyond that, look, we have these independent businesses which each have their own long-range plans and so they're using those long-range plans to project forward and we plan for compute for all of them.
zh: 除此之外，你看，我们有这些独立的业务，每项业务都有自己的长期规划，它们用这些长期规划来向前预测，而我们为所有这些业务规划算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the cloud team, they have a business and they have a projection and they have demand signals, they've committed contracts.
zh: 所以云团队，他们有一项业务，他们有一个预测，他们有需求信号，他们有已签订的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with that help, we can plan on a long-term compute trajectory for them.
zh: 有了这些帮助，我们就可以为他们规划长期的算力轨迹。

zh: 我觉得我们很幸运能有这么广泛的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's no company in the world which isn't making trade-offs at any given moment in time.
zh: 我认为世界上没有任何一家公司在任何给定时刻不在做取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the first principles we operate on is to making sure we have enough compute to invest in the frontier.
zh: 但我们运营的第一性原则是确保我们有足够的算力投入到前沿领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's non-negotiable and everything else works on top of it.
zh: 那是不可谈判的，其他一切都建立在这之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what you're seeing in these conversations is if you sit now, remember, we are building our own compute, our own data centers.

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's long lead times.
zh: 所以有很长的前置时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the compute we have today is a function of decisions I made in 2024.

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if you think back to a year from today, last year, the agent recording takeoff hadn't happened.

speaker: Unknown
en: So today, obviously, when you sit and look at anything, everyone is short, not just us, other companies, and everyone wishes you had 2X of what you had planned for.
zh: 所以今天，显然，当你坐下来审视任何东西时，每个人都短缺，不只是我们，其他公司也一样，每个人都希望你拥有的比计划的多 2 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that comes with the territory, right?
zh: 我想这是伴随这个领域而来的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And at any given moment in time, we are planning for what we would need two to three years out in the future.
zh: 而在任何给定时刻，我们都在为未来两到三年所需要的东西做规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you're going to find some decisions you make may look suboptimal two years out, depending on where the state of the art is.
zh: 所以我想你会发现，你做出的某些决策在两年后可能看起来不够最优，取决于当时最先进技术处于什么状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't spend too much time thinking about it.
zh: 所以我不会花太多时间去想这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I think about computer allocation is making sure Google DeepMind, both for research and frontier model development, is cutting edge in terms of compute access.

speaker: Unknown
en: And after that, we plan for all our businesses.
zh: 在那之后,我们再为所有业务做规划。

en: Briefly, there was a podcast where Ben Horowitz relayed that Andy Jassy had said something like, computers sold out till 2028.

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there's part of the reason even last year we went out and leased some short-term compute was to accommodate some customers and help them out.
zh: 你知道,这也是为什么甚至去年我们出去租了一些短期算力,部分原因就是为了满足一些客户的需求、帮他们一把。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yes, I think we are all dealing with similar timelines.
zh: 但是是的,我认为我们都在应对类似的时间线。

en: One bubble question.

zh: 这取决于你看的时间跨度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we...

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, this level of build, you know, if I take a long enough timeframe, it makes complete sense to me.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们处于有史以来最重要的技术的早期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is not like fiber.
zh: 而且这不像光纤。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not dark.
zh: 它不是暗光纤。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are using it.
zh: 我们在用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are capacity constrained on a daily basis.
zh: 我们每天都在面临容量受限。

speaker: Unknown
en: The applications, the underlying technology is improving rapidly, right?
zh: 这些应用、底层技术正在快速进步,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But...
zh: 但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Running a company, the way I work through the moment is you look at your demand signals.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 看你以合同形式获得的已承诺的收入机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: You balance that with the underlying technical capability, our internal evals, how we are using it internally, the model trajectories.
zh: 再把它与底层技术能力、我们的内部评测、我们内部是如何使用它的、模型轨迹相平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And based on all that, you take a disciplined approach, a confident, aggressive, but a disciplined approach to plan out compute.
zh: 基于这一切,你采取一种有纪律的方式,一种自信、进取但有纪律的方式去规划算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you talk about the broader economy as a whole, you're having people operate with various levels of risk.
zh: 但当你谈论整个更广泛的经济体时,人们是在以不同程度的风险在运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: I focus on what I can control as a company and plan through it.
zh: 我专注于作为一家公司我能控制的东西,并据此进行规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your question is, can there be an overbuild?
zh: 如果你问的是,会不会出现过度建设?

en: Yes, because you can have some constrained components.
zh: 会的,因为某些组件可能会有约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: And remember, what matters is a square set of everything you need to build out that compute.
zh: 而且记住,关键在于你要建成那套算力所需的一切要素是不是齐全的一整套。

speaker: Unknown
en: Memory, electricity, electricians, land.
zh: 内存、电力、电工、土地。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are like 2,000 components or more, right?
zh: 大概有 2000 个或更多的组件,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you could get constrained at some point.
zh: 所以你可能在某个环节受到约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: There could be things which cause bottlenecks, and then you could have overbuilds.
zh: 可能会有造成瓶颈的因素,然后就可能出现过度建设。

speaker: Unknown
en: There could be external shocks to the economy, et cetera.
zh: 也可能有来自经济的外部冲击,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are macro risks.
zh: 所以存在宏观风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: All that is possible at any given time.
zh: 这些在任何时候都有可能发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But am I confident that the compute we are planning for, we will have uses for it given enough time?
zh: 但我是否相信,我们正在规划的算力,在足够长的时间里会有它的用武之地?

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely, yes.
zh: 当然,是的。

en: Okay, one more on this.

zh: 而如果你是这样的人——我当时就在现场,你说 AI 会像火和电一样影响深远,我们都笑了,现在我有点后悔那声笑——

en: But if you're someone that actually believes that,
zh: 但如果你是这样真正相信的人,

en: then the thinking would be you give the researchers the biggest possible computer even if it is to the detriment of today's profits like the cloud business.
zh: 那么思路就会是,给研究者最大的计算机,即使这会损害今天的利润,比如云业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your thoughts.

en: We're all doing some form of that, right?
zh: 我们都在做某种形式的事情,对吧?

en: I think our cloud business is at any given moment in time foregoing short-term revenues because we are making compute trade-offs to support frontier AI development.

en: You know, that's what helps you come with a more efficient algorithmic breakthrough, maybe to use less memory, et cetera.
